elements.element: Customer is not bound by any exclusivity obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly appoints Vendor as a “non-exclusive provider,” and Section 12.3 states that nothing restricts Customer from engaging any supplier and that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: Customer is not obligated to use Vendor as its sole supplier.
elements.evidence: The sole-provider language was removed from Section 2.2. Section 12.3 also preserves Customer’s right to engage any supplier.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation binding Customer is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer, so the condition requiring a product-category limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation binding Customer lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer, so there is no exclusivity period exceeding the permitted 12-month maximum.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer; therefore, there is no exclusivity obligation requiring termination upon this trigger.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer; therefore, there is no exclusivity obligation requiring termination upon this trigger.

result.reason: The operative revision removes the sole-and-exclusive appointment and replaces it with an express non-exclusive appointment, reinforced by Section 12.3. This fully achieves the preferred position and necessarily satisfies the fallback’s maximum restrictions because no exclusivity obligation exists. The change is narrowly targeted and introduces no contradiction or unrelated commercial term.
